title: Studying Scripture
definition: Studying Scripture is the careful, prayerful pursuit of understanding God’s Word so believers may know truth, follow Christ, and teach faithfully.
summary: Studying Scripture is the careful, prayerful pursuit of understanding God’s Word so believers may know truth, follow Christ, and teach faithfully.
christFocus: Jesus opened the Scriptures to reveal Himself, and faithful study helps believers see Christ more clearly and walk in His ways.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Studying Scripture means giving attention to what God has actually said. It involves reading carefully, observing context, asking good questions, comparing Scripture with Scripture, and seeking the Lord’s help rather than forcing personal opinions onto the text.

Bible study is not only for pastors or advanced students. Every believer needs the Word of God. A person in recovery needs truth stronger than cravings. A church-hurt person needs Scripture without manipulation. A teacher needs the Word before speaking to others. A new believer needs steady grounding in Christ.

The goal of study is not pride, argument, or information hoarding. The goal is to know God, behold Christ, be shaped by the Spirit, and obey the Word. Good study should make believers more humble, more faithful, and more ready to serve.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people either avoid Scripture because they feel unqualified or misuse Scripture because they read too quickly and without care. Studying Scripture guards against both neglect and careless handling.

This doctrine corrects the idea that spiritual growth happens only through emotion, experience, or inspiration. God forms His people through truth understood, believed, and obeyed.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Set aside time to study Scripture with prayer and humility. Look at the passage, its context, its meaning, and its connection to Christ, then ask how the Holy Spirit is calling you to trust, repent, obey, teach, or encourage someone else.
